title: Graph of ordered pairs as a relationship between two variables
summary: Connect inputs and outputs in tables, ordered pairs, rules and contextual graphs.
objectives: Interpret an ordered pair as an input-output relationship.
Complete tables and ordered-pair patterns from a rule.
Derive and use a simple linear rule from values or context.

blocks.text: A relationship can be shown by a rule, a table, a set of ordered pairs or a graph. Each ordered pair (x, y) links one input x to its output y. Moving between these representations should preserve every pair.
For a linear relationship, equal changes in x produce equal changes in y. This constant change helps extend a table and identify the rule.

sections.title: Build a rule from ordered pairs

prompt.text: The pairs (0, 2), (1, 6) and (2, 10) follow a linear relationship. Write y as an expression in x.

content.text: Find the change in output for an input increase of 1.
Use x = 0 to read the constant output.

sections.verification_note: Substitution gives outputs 2, 6 and 10 for x = 0, 1 and 2 respectively.

prompt.text: For y = 3x - 1, find y when x = 5.

blocks.text: Treat x as the input and y as the output; check that a rule reproduces every given ordered pair.
